newsitem.title: GERMANY: Agents warn Lufthansa over commission cut.
newsitem.headline: Agents warn Lufthansa over commission cut.

text.p: Travel agents in Germany are threatening to switch bookings away from Deutsche Lufthansa AG over cuts in commission payments, industry association ASR said on Monday.
Agents were angry at a cut to five percent commission for domestic German flights from nine percent due to come into effect in May, the agents' association said.
At a snow-hit meeting in Frankfurt, 28 of 39 IATA travel agents in attendance warned in a survey that the new Lufthansa agents' payment structure no longer made it worth selling Lufthansa tickets.
They would reduce Lufthansa sales and switch bookings to rival airlines, they said.
Only one agent described the Lufthansa system as a fair offer for agents and all but two claimed the five percent commission for domestic German flights did not cover costs.
The 39 agencies represented an estimated total buying power of more than 40 million marks, the survey indicated.
Lufthansa Germany passenger sales manager Stefan Pichler told the meeting that 871 agents had already signed the new Lufthansa agency contracts.

Under the new commissions system valid from May 1, the previous nine percent flat rate will be replaced by a two-tier system of nine percent for international ticket sales and five percent for domestic flights.
In addition, performance-related incentives will be paid acccording to sales volume, selected destinations and use of electronic booking technology.
